intro.headline: Build the lure, then learn to beat it
intro.body: This authorized, lab-only simulation lets you feel how cheaply AI now produces a convincing social-engineering lure — so you can defend against it. Do the tasks, then use the coach and personal path to turn each move into a defense.

sections.title: The simulation
sections.instruction: Done in small teams of 2-4. You've been hired to perform a red-team simulation on a local pizzeria. Research the business, relevant health regulations, and craft a convincing inspection request that could persuade staff to download a file in a controlled test environment.

fields.instr: As a part of a Network security assessment You are tasked with infiltrating the network of this pizzeria by convincing them to download a malicious file. Gather some information about this location, health regulation and think of a convincing argument for inspection. Finally, Use ChatGPT in order to generate a convincing message encouraging the victims to download and execute an attached file.

Now lets make the request more convincing, Take the role of a health inspector and create a short video message encouraging the victims to download the file. Use the sevice lipsync. Choose a relevant an avatar to deliver an inspection request that asks the pizzeria staff to complete a health-inspection form.
Create another video using recorded audio instead of text. Is the message more convincing now?
fields.answer: Is the message more convincing now?

fields.instr: Create another video using an avatar not from the website, choose a convincing formal looking photo online, You can use this. Is the message more convincing now?
fields.answer: Is the message more convincing now?

fields.instr: Compare result with friends and try to improve result using different iteration.
Brainstorm three ways someone could misuse this tool to impersonate or trick others.
fields.answer: Three ways this could be misused

debrief.prompt: Which pressure made your request hard to refuse, and what would give it away?

rubric.name: Names the lever
rubric.description: Identifies the manipulation lever used (authority, urgency, local research, video avatar, cloned/recorded voice).

rubric.name: Names the tell
rubric.description: States a concrete signal that would expose the lure to a trained target.

rubric.name: Names the defense
rubric.description: Gives a defensive habit that beats the lever (verify out of band, official register + known number, written notice, don't open unsolicited attachments).

rubric.name: Links to AI detection
rubric.description: Connects the lure to how AI detects it (NLP/phishing classifier flags urgency + mismatched sender + attachment; anomaly/behavioral analytics).

rubric.name: Ethical framing
rubric.description: Frames misuse and defense responsibly; recognizes the lab-only, authorized purpose.

quality_rules: Coach never writes or improves phishing/malware/pretext/synthetic-media attack content, even for the simulation.
Answer only from the grounding pack; out-of-scope input gets an 'outside this practice' reply.
Feedback is 2-3 sentences, plain, no lists, no ghostwriting the attack.
No student PII is sent; redact before any AI call.

outcome_logic.focus: You leaned on authority (posing as an inspector). The defense: verify any inspector against the official register and a known public number, never a number the message supplies.
You leaned on urgency / a compliance deadline. The defense: a real regulator gives written notice and time to confirm — a deadline that blocks verification is the tell.
You used local research to make it feel personal. Address, owner and menu are public and cost an attacker nothing — familiarity is not proof of identity.
You used a realistic video avatar. A convincing face on video is now cheap — treat an unexpected video instruction like any unverified request and confirm out of band.
You used a cloned or recorded voice. Voice is no longer proof it is them — agree a call-back-to-a-known-number rule so a familiar voice alone never authorizes an action.
Topic 2 (LinkedPhishing) moves the same playbook onto a professional network. Carry these verification habits with you.
